final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is substantively more careful than a controls-cure theory, but it still does not satisfy the missing compliance predicate identified in the initial audit: admissible proof of explicit pre-launch disclosure or approved risk acceptance covering the exposed fraud dispute review segment. The evidence supports aggregate readiness and controllable rollout, but policy and the quoted rollout-control rule both preserve the disclosure duty when the affected use case remains exposed. On this record, a present-tense compliance finding would still overreach. The most defensible audit outcome remains suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats, because the caveat here is not merely explanatory; it is an unresolved policy condition that must be evidenced before launch.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows the required pre-launch model-card disclosure for the fraud dispute review limitation exists.
No admissible approval shows certification is formally conditioned on that disclosure being present before launch.
The exposed fraud dispute review segment remains in the initial rollout cohort, so rollout percentage, rollback, and monitoring do not satisfy the disclosure predicate.
The only risk-acceptance item is an unapproved draft with a blank approver line and no express coverage of fraud dispute review exposure.
